newsitem.title: JAPAN: Supertanker spills oil in Tokyo Bay.
newsitem.headline: Supertanker spills oil in Tokyo Bay.

text.p: A supertanker spilled crude oil after scraping a reef in shallow waters of Tokyo Bay on Wednesday morning, Japan's coast guard said.
It was unclear how much crude oil had spilled into the bay or whether the flow had stopped, said a spokesman for the coast guard, called the Maritime Safety Agency (MSA).

NHK public television said, however, that the leaked crude amounted to 7,400 kilolitres, or about 6,300 tonnes, which would make it one of Japan's worst ever oil spills. The worst spill was in January, when a Russian tanker carrying 19,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil broke in half in the Sea of Japan.

The very large crude carrier (VLCC) was on its way to a refinery in Kawasaki, south of Tokyo, belonging to Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd. The 259,999 deadweight tonne Panamanian-flagged Diamond Grace was carrying about 257,000 tonnes of crude from the United Arab Emirates, a company spokesman said.
Earlier, the tanker was reported to be 255,000 deadweight tonnes.
The Mitsubishi spokesman said it was unclear how the accident might affect operations at the 75,000 barrel-per-day Kawasaki refinery.
The coast guard said a film of crude about six km (3.75 miles) in length was spreading.
Japanese media reports said the oil slick was about 150 metres (yards) wide, and that an oil fence had been erected around the tanker to stop oil from spreading.
NHK said none of the 26-member crew had been injured and they were still on board the vessel.
It said oil had apparently spilled from two cracks on the right side of the tanker's bow.
